QASHANI:84:16-21/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:16-21/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:16-21/r5.claim: The reminder of these states should make listeners submit to the Qur’an; those veiled from truth remain necessarily veiled from religion.
QASHANI:84:16-21/r5.anchor: بتذكير هذه الأطوار والمراتب لا يخضعون ولا ينقادون

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.claim: Physical phenomena show gradual change under God's control; humanity too steadily moves toward meeting its Lord, so denying that outcome is foolish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p238/r1.anchor: everything at all times is in the grasp of God. Man too is gradually moving forward to meet his Lord

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r3.claim: Not prostrating before the Quran means refusing inward humility and submission to truth, and therefore also refusing the ritual prostration required when it is recited.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r3.anchor: أي يخضعون بالقلب ويتذللون للحق بالسجود اللغوي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r4.claim: The Quran contains comprehensive worldly and afterlife benefits, distinguishes lawful from unlawful, and bears self-evident testimony to its divine origin and miraculousness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p373#s084/r4.anchor: الجامع لكل ما ينفعهم في دنياهم وأخراهم الفارق بين كل ملتبس من الحرام والحلال

ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r14.claim: When the Quran is recited, they neither prostrate nor submit to its truth and commands.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r14.anchor: secde etmezler boyun eğmezler, hakikati [5684] teslim etmezler

ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r15.claim: A report says the Prophet recited 96:19 and prostrated, the believers followed, and Quraysh clapped and whistled; the verse was then revealed.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r15.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselam bir gün وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب [el-Alâk 96/19] okumuş da secde etmiş

ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r16.claim: Abu Hanifa infers that prostration at this recitation is obligatory, while Shafii calls it Sunnah; Ibn Abbas is reported to deny prostrations in the Mufassal surahs.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r16.anchor: İmâm-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe Hazretleri bununla burada secde-i tilâvetin vücûbuna istidlâl eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r17.claim: Abu Hurayra swore that he prostrated after seeing the Prophet do so here; Anas says Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali also prostrated in prayer.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r17.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre radıyallahu anh burada secde etmiş ve

ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r18.claim: If the surah is recited through its end before bowing, the prayer’s bowing and prostration suffice for the recitation prostration; Hasan’s report that it is not obligatory is understood this way.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#5/r18.anchor: sûrenin, âhirine kadar okunup da rükû‘a gidilecek olursa namazın rükû‘ve sücûduyla secde-i tilâvet sâkıt olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r16.claim: Despite the evidence, disbelievers are rebuked for not believing and not prostrating in reverence when the Qur'an is recited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r16.anchor: inkârcılar, hâlâ inanmadıkları ve Kur’an okunduğunda Allah’a saygı ile secde etmedikleri için 20 ve 21. âyetlerdeki soruyla kınanmışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r17.claim: Reports of the Prophet's practice led to three legal views on prostration at this verse: obligatory, sunnah, or neither.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:84:16/r17.anchor: “Vâciptir” veya “sünnettir” diyenler olduğu gibi “ne vâcip ne sünnettir” diyenler de vardır

NAHHAS:v5p188/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p188/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v5p188/r5.claim: Exegetes agree that they do not humble themselves by submitting to God’s obedience.
NAHHAS:v5p188/r5.anchor: أهل التفسير على أن المعنى لا يخضعون ولا يذلون بالانتهاء إلى طاعة الله

TABRISI:84:24-25/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:24-25/r5.claim: Asking why deniers do not believe or prostrate shows these are their own actions: a wise speaker would not demand what someone cannot do.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r5.anchor: دلالة على أن الإيمان والسجود فعلهم لأن الحكيم لا يقول ما لك

TABRISI:84:24-25/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:24-25/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:24-25/r6.claim: The verse also shows that unbelievers are addressed by the obligations of worship.
TABRISI:84:24-25/r6.anchor: ويدل قوله { لا يسجدون } على أن الكفار مخاطبون بالعبادات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r3.claim: When the Qur'an announces this great truth, prostration should express gratitude for its greatness and news; their arrogant denial reverses that proper response.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r3.anchor: it was only befitting for them to have

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r4.claim: Arabs and Egyptians would prostrate to acknowledge impressive discourse; the author cites Pharaoh's magicians and poets who prostrated on hearing Labid as examples.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p247/r4.anchor: Here worth considering the fact is a tradition of the Arabs

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet recited al-ʿAlaq 96:19 and prostrated with the believers while Quraysh clapped overhead, after which this verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r2.anchor: فسجد بمن معه من المؤمنين وقريش تصفق فوق رؤوسهم فنزلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah cites the rebuke of those who heard but did not prostrate as proof that recitation prostration is obligatory.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r3.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة على وجوب السجود فإنه ذم لمن سمعه ولم يسجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r4.claim: Abū Hurayrah says he prostrated at this passage only after seeing the Messenger prostrate there.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:20-25/r4.anchor: أنه سجد فيها وقال: والله ما سجدت فيها إلا بعد

STUDYQURAN:84:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r1.claim: The Quran is another sign of God: those who fail to read created signs should recognize the Quran's miracle and its signs.
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r1.anchor: Here the Quran is invoked as another sign of God, as if to say, “If they cannot read the signs of God in the created world

STUDYQURAN:84:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r2.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r2.claim: Some take prostrating to mean prayer.

STUDYQURAN:84:21/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r3.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r3.claim: Others take prostrating to mean humility.
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r3.anchor: Others say it refers to humility

STUDYQURAN:84:21/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r4.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r4.claim: Most commentators count this among fifteen verses after which one prostrates when reciting the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r4.anchor: Most maintain that this is one of fifteen verses after which one prostrates when reciting the Quran

STUDYQURAN:84:21/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r5.speaker: Imam Mālik and other Mālikī jurists
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r5.claim: Imam Mālik does not require prostration after this verse, while other Mālikī jurists do.
STUDYQURAN:84:21/r5.anchor: Imam Mālik does not maintain that one is obligated to prostrate after reciting this verse, but other Mālikī jurists do

TABRISI:84:20-23/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:20-23/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:20-23/r9.claim: The question continues: what prevents them from believing and prostrating to God when the Qurʾan is recited?
TABRISI:84:20-23/r9.anchor: أي ما الذي يصرفهم عن الإيمان وعن السجود لله تعالى

TABRISI:84:20-23/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:20-23/r10.speaker: عطاء والكلبي
TABRISI:84:20-23/r10.claim: ʿAta and al-Kalbi interpret their not prostrating as not praying to God.
TABRISI:84:20-23/r10.anchor: وقيل: معنى لا يسجدون لا يصلون لله تعالى عن عطاء والكلبي

TABRISI:84:20-23/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:20-23/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABRISI:84:20-23/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited إذا السماء انشقت and prostrated.
TABRISI:84:20-23/r11.anchor: وفي خبر مرفوع عن أبي هريرة قال قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v10p295/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p295/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p295/r10.claim: The conditional clause is circumstantial and coordinated with the preceding clause, describing their state when the Qur'an is recited to them.
BURSEVI:v10p295/r10.anchor: جملة شرطية محلها النصب على الحالية نسقا على ما قبلها

BURSEVI:v10p295/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p295/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p295/r11.claim: Their failure to bow or submit when the Prophet, one of his Companions, or another Muslim recites the Qur'an is blameworthy: as speakers of Arabic, they should recognize its inimitability and divine origin, affirm Muhammad's prophethood, and obey him.
BURSEVI:v10p295/r11.anchor: أي أي مانع لهم حال عدم سجودهم وخضوعهم واستكانتهم عند قراءة النبي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p295/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p295/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p295/r12.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means not performing prostration when the specific prostration verse is recited, rather than failing to prostrate at any Qur'an recitation.
BURSEVI:v10p295/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد به نفس السجود عند تلاوة آية السجدة على أن يكون المراد

THALABI:v10p162/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p162/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p162/r9.claim: The unbelievers do not humble themselves or yield when the Quran is recited to them.
THALABI:v10p162/r9.anchor: فما لهم لا يؤمنون وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون لا يخضعون ولا يستكينون له

THALABI:v10p162/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p162/r10.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v10p162/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil interpret “do not prostrate” as “do not pray.”

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r9.speaker: عطاء والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Kalbī explain their not prostrating as not praying to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r9.anchor: قال عطاء (¬6)، والكلبي (¬7): لا يصلون لله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r10.speaker: غيرهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r10.claim: Other interpreters say it means they do not humble themselves or submit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p372/r10.anchor: وقال غيرهم (¬1): لا يخضعون، ولا يستكينون

BURHAN:v2p116/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p116/r1.claim: Abu Bakr argues that if eloquent opponents had thought the Qur’an was poetry, they would have challenged it, since poetry was accessible; their failure shows they did not regard it as poetry.
BURHAN:v2p116/r1.anchor: فالجواب قال القاضي أبو بكر إن الفصحاء منهم

BURHAN:v2p116/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p116/r2.claim: It is implausible that the masters of Arabic rhetoric missed poetry in the Qur’an while later readers detected it, given their strong motive to discredit it.
BURHAN:v2p116/r2.anchor: فمن استدرك فيه شعرا زعم أنه خفي على أولئك النفر وهم ملوك الكلام

BURHAN:v2p116/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r3.speaker: أكثر أهل صناعة العربية
BURHAN:v2p116/r3.claim: Most Muslim Arabic specialists say a single metrical line is not poetry; poetry requires at least two lines, and two lines with different meters and rhymes are not poetry.
BURHAN:v2p116/r3.anchor: وقالوا أيضا إن ما كان على وزن بيتين إلا أنه يختلف وزنهما وقافيتهما فليس بشعر أصلا

BURHAN:v2p116/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r4.speaker: قوم
BURHAN:v2p116/r4.claim: Some deny that rajaz is poetry, especially when it is a half-line or fragment; others require at least four rajaz lines, which the Qur’an does not contain.
BURHAN:v2p116/r4.anchor: ثم منهم من قال إن الرلجز ليس بشعر أصلا

BURHAN:v2p116/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p116/r5.claim: Poetry requires deliberate use of a poetic method; accidental meter in ordinary speech does not make every speaker a poet.
BURHAN:v2p116/r5.anchor: ثم يقول إن الشعر إنما ينطلق متى قصد إليه على الطريق التي تعمد وتسلك ولا يصح أن يتفق مثله إلا من الشعراء

BURHAN:v2p116/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p116/r6.claim: Abu Bakr considers this defense reliable or mostly so and adds that people would naturally try to rival poetry, which is not intractable for contemporaries.
BURHAN:v2p116/r6.anchor: قال القاضي وهذه الطريق التي سلكوها في الجواب معتمدة أو أكثرها ولو كان ذلك شعرا لكانت النفوس تتشوق إلى معارضته

BURHAN:v2p116/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p116/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p116/r7.claim: A facet of inimitability is varying register and placing the wording suited to each situation; replacing a word with a synonym removes its elegance and sweetness.
BURHAN:v2p116/r7.anchor: مما يبعث على معرفة الإعجاز اختلافات المقامات وذكر في كل موضع ما يلائمه

SAMIN-DURR:84:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:21/r1.claim: إذا قرئ is a condition and لا يسجدون its answer; the conditional clause is also a circumstantial accusative coordinated with what precedes, asking why they do not prostrate when the Quran is recited.
SAMIN-DURR:84:21/r1.anchor: قوله: { وإذا قرىء }: شرط، و " لا يسجدون ". جوابه. وهذه الجملة الشرطية في محل نصب على الحال أيضا نسقا على ما قبلها، أي: فمالهم إذا قرىء عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون؟

ASAD-NOTES:84:16#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:84:16#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:84:16#n12/r1.claim: Asad explains the Qur'an's call to prostration by its consistent stress on God's law of unceasing change and progression throughout existence.
ASAD-NOTES:84:16#n12/r1.anchor: seeing how consistently it stresses the divine law of unceasing change and progression in all that exists

QIRAAT-ER:84:21:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:3#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:3#1/r1.claim: Hamza easing changes passive quriʾa to quriya by smoothing the final hamza, without changing the passive sense.
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:3#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza easing: قُرِئَ (quriʾa) is read قُرِيَ (quriya), smoothing the final hamza

QIRAAT-ER:84:21:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:5#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:5#1/r1.claim: The noun al-qurʾānu is read al-qurānu with hamza easing, preserving the same referent.
QIRAAT-ER:84:21:5#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza easing in the noun: ٱلْقُرْءَانُ (al-qurʾānu) is read ٱلْقُرَانُ (al-qurānu)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil gloss their failure to prostrate as failure to pray.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r3.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Companions prostrated with the Prophet during recitation of al-ʿAlaq and al-Inshiqāq; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سجدنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r4.speaker: أبو رافع
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r4.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ says he prayed the night prayer behind Abū Hurayra, who prostrated after reciting al-Inshiqāq and said he had prostrated behind the Prophet and would continue doing so until they met.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p376/r4.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال: صليت مع أبي هريرة العتمة فقرأ إذا السماء انشقت، فسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r4.claim: لا يسجدون is coordinated with لا يؤمنون.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r4.anchor: لا يسجدون } عطف على { لا يؤمنون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r5.claim: The introductory time clause is fronted to emphasize and honor the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r5.anchor: ظرف قدم على عامله للاهتمام به وتنويه شأن القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r6.claim: Reciting the Quran to them means recitation to convey the message and invite them to faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r6.anchor: وقراءة القرآن عليهم قراءته قراءة تبليغ ودعوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r7.claim: Ibn Ubayy told the Prophet not to deceive or provoke them with Quran during their gatherings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r7.anchor: عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول : ( لا تغشنا به في مجالسنا )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r8.claim: The Prophet recited Quran to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, as Ibn Ashur discussed under Surat Abasa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r8.anchor: وقرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن على الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r9.claim: Sajdah means submission and humility: they do not submit to God, the Quran’s meanings, or its proof, nor believe its truth, as contrasted with their denial in 84:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r9.anchor: والسجود مستعمل بمعنى الخضوع والخشوع كقوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r10.claim: The wording does not establish a Quranic prostration at this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r10.anchor: وليس في هذه الآية ما يقتضي أن عند هذه الآية سجدة من سجود القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r11.claim: Ibn Ashur considers the stronger Maliki position to be that this is not one of the Quran’s prostration verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r11.anchor: الأصح من قول مالك وأصحابه أنها ليست من سجود القرآن خلافا لابن وهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r12.speaker: ابن وهب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r12.claim: Ibn Wahb, a Maliki, counts fourteen Quranic prostrations, including this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r12.anchor: خلافا لابن وهب من أصحاب مالك فإنه جعل سجودات القرآن أربع عشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r13.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r13.claim: Al-Shafi‘i holds that prostration here is recommended.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r14.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r14.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that prostration here is obligatory.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r15.claim: Ibn Ashur judges that eleven prostrations are established by sound reports from Companions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r15.anchor: والأرجح أن عزائم السجود المسنونة إحدى عشرة سجدة وهي التي رويت بالأسانيد الصحيحة عن الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r16.claim: Reports say the Prophet prostrated at three additional verses including this one, but other reports conflict; Ibn Ashur allows that he left the prostration or did not emphasize it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r16.anchor: ثلاث آيات غير الإحدى عشرة آية رويت فيها أخبار أنها سجد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند قراءتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r17.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r17.claim: Ibn al-Arabi identifies prostration at Surat al-Inshiqaq as the position of the Medinan Malikis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p231/r17.anchor: وقال ابن العربي السجود في سورة الانشقاق قول المدنيين من أصحاب مالك

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r3.claim: One explanation says they do not humble themselves when the Qur’an is recited.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r3.anchor: وإذا قرئ عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون قيل: لا يخضعون.

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r4.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil understand the verse as asking why they do not pray and humble themselves when the Qur’an is recited.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r4.anchor: وقيل: ما لهم لا يصلون، عن الكلبي، ومقاتل. أي: ما الذي يمنعهم من الصلاة، والخضوع عند القرآن.

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r18.claim: The questions show that unbelievers can choose faith and prostration and that these acts are theirs, against the determinists: one cannot ask why someone failed to do what he could not do.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r18.anchor: أنهم: قادرون على الإيمان، والإيمان فعلهم، خلاف قول المجبرة؛

JISHUMI:v10p7346/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r19.claim: The verse shows that unbelievers are addressed by religious duties and establishes a required prostration here; Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet recited this sūra and prostrated.
JISHUMI:v10p7346/r19.anchor: ويدل قوله: لا يسجدون أن الكفار مخاطبون بالشرائع، ويدل أن هاهنا سجدة واجبة. وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قرأ هذه السورة وسجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r10.claim: The statement means that they do not pray.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r10.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذا قرىء عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون } أي لا يصلون

QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r11.claim: In a sound report, Abu Hurayrah recited “When the sky is split open” and prostrated; afterward he told the people that the Prophet had prostrated at this passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r11.anchor: وفي الصحيح: إن أبا هريرة قرأ { إذا السمآء انشقت } فسجد فيها، فلما انصرف أخبرهم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سجد فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r12.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r12.claim: Malik says this is not one of the obligatory prostration passages, because the meaning is that they do not submit or obey its required actions.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r12.anchor: وقد قال مالك: إنها ليست من عزائم السجود لأن المعنى لا يذعنون ولا يطيعون في العمل بواجباته

QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r13.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says it is an obligatory prostration passage, as in the Medinese report from Malik, supported by Qur'an and Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r13.anchor: ابن العربي: والصحيح أنها منه، وهي رواية المدنيين عنه، وقد اعتضد فيها القرآن والسنة

QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r14.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r14.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says he avoided reciting the passage when leading people: prostrating would be rejected, while omitting it would be a shortcoming, so he recited it only when praying alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:19-21/r14.anchor: قال ابن العربي: لما أممت بالناس تركت قراءتها لأني إن سجدت أنكروه، وإن تركتها كان تقصيرا مني
